title: Cumberland Pie
subtitle: A minced beef and vegetable pie topped with mashed potato and a cheddar crust
excerpt: Rich minced beef and vegetables in a thick gravy, covered with a mash topping and a layer of grated cheddar. A close relative of cottage pie, with a crunchier golden finish.
sourceNotes: A British variant of cottage pie, traditionally distinguished by its breadcrumb or cheese-topped mash; this version uses mature cheddar.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze before the final bake. Defrost overnight in the fridge and bake at 190C for 35 to 40 minutes until piping hot.
recipe.batchNotes: This recipe doubles well in a large roasting tin. Portion and freeze in family-sized amounts.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble the full pie up to two days ahead. Keep covered in the fridge and add 10 minutes to the baking time.

content.text: Cumberland pie sits in the same family as cottage pie but the topping is creamier mash with a layer of cheddar that forms a proper crust in the oven. The filling needs to be well-seasoned and the gravy reduced before the mash goes on top. A loose, wet filling will make the topping sink.
Heat the oil in the frying pan over a high heat. Brown the mince in two batches without stirring until properly coloured. Remove and set aside.
Reduce the heat to medium. Soften the onion, carrot, and celery in the same pan for 7 minutes. Stir in the tomato puree and cook for 1 minute. Add the flour and stir for 30 seconds.

Return the mince to the pan. Pour in the stock and add the Worcestershire sauce and thyme. Stir well, season generously, and bring to a simmer. Cover and cook for 25 minutes. Uncover and cook for a further 5 minutes to reduce the gravy. Remove the thyme.
While the filling cooks, boil the potatoes in well-salted water until completely tender. Drain and mash with the butter and warm milk until smooth. Season with salt and white pepper.

Heat the oven to 190C. Tip the filling into a large baking dish or roasting tin. Spoon the mash over the top and spread evenly with a fork or the back of a spoon, running the fork across to create ridges.
Scatter the grated cheddar evenly over the mash. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the cheese is golden and the filling is bubbling around the edges.

items.symptom: The mash sinks into the filling.
items.cause: The filling was too loose when the mash was applied.
items.fix: Reduce the filling until it holds a shape on a spoon before topping. Let it cool for 5 minutes before spooning the mash over.

items.symptom: The cheddar is pale rather than golden.
items.cause: The oven was not hot enough or the pie was taken out too early.
items.fix: Switch on the grill for the final 3 to 4 minutes, watching closely to avoid burning.

items.symptom: The mash topping is stiff and gluey.
items.cause: The potatoes were over-worked or the milk was cold.
items.fix: Add warm milk in stages and mash by hand. Do not use a blender or food processor; they make mash paste.
